summary: Transient prefetch lock contention causing periodic p99 latency spikes for short streaming requests
description:
Issue summary:
Transient contention on the prefetch/kv-cache lock in the continuous batcher is causing periodic p99 latency spikes (and occasional request timeouts) for short streaming connections. This manifests as ~1–2 minute windows where many short requests (single-turn streaming with small prompt length) see p95/p99 climb from baseline ~80ms/220ms to 700ms–3s and some 504/timeout errors.

Impact:
- Customer AppScribe (dedicated) experiencing user-visible slowdowns in transcription preview and occasional failed streaming responses.
- Roughly 2–4% of requests during affected windows hit >2s latency, causing user retries.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, Dedicated pool charmed-redwood-03
- Affected model variants: redwood-optimized-7b (default), fallback llama2-13b-quant

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Idle period of service for ~5–20 minutes (low QPS).
2) Traffic resumes with many short streaming requests (avg prompt tokens < 32).
3) P99 climbs in waves for 60–120s, then decays to baseline.
4) Repeatable when we replay a short-request trace at ~120–200 rps for 30s after an idle window.

Observed behavior / evidence:
- Metric correlation: p99 spikes align with elevated "prefetch-lock-wait-ms" histogram on batcher host nodes.
- Logs (samples):
  [2026-03-01T14:12:07.342Z] request_id=aa3f7 prefetch_wait_ms=512 batch_flush_id=9882 stream_conn=stream-71 status=queued
  [2026-03-01T14:12:07.856Z] request_id=aa3f7 kv_prefill_status=delayed flush_duration_ms=740 status=flushed
  [2026-03-01T14:12:08.013Z] request_id=bb9c1 error=504 deadline_exceeded
- Sampling of stack traces during spike shows contention on PrefetchManager::acquire_prefill_lock and subsequent wait on condition variable.
- We see prefetched KV misses more often during spikes (cache_warm_ratio drops to ~30% from baseline ~85%).

Hypothesis:
- When the continuous batcher resumes after idle, a small subset of requests trigger prefetch routines concurrently. A separated codepath uses a coarse-grained prefill lock that serializes kv-cache prefill across in-flight streams. Under certain timing, this serial prefill blocks the batcher flush path, increasing end-to-end latency and creating a positive feedback loop as delayed flushes queue more short requests.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Reduce per-connection streaming concurrency (client-side) and enable a short keepalive/ping to avoid long idle windows (>5m) while we investigate. Applied on 2026-03-01 16:40 UTC. This reduced spike amplitude but did not fully eliminate windows.

Next steps planned:
1) Instrumentation: add per-request prefill lock wait metric and trace tag (short-term PR).
2) Code change: refactor PrefetchManager to use sharded locks or optimistic prefill to avoid global serialization. Target PR: runtime/prefetch-shard (draft).
3) Deploy canary patch to prod-us-east on a small subset of hosts and measure p99.
4) Customer follow-up: coordinate a quiet-window replay test at low-risk hour.

Attachments / links:
- Dashboards: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/abcd/prefetch-locks?orgId=1
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1642-prefetch-latency
- Snapshot logs: s3://redwood-support/sup-584391/logsnap-20260301.tar.gz
